LeafFilter and LeafGuard are two of the biggest brands in gutter protection, but they take very different approaches. 

LeafFilter is a micro-mesh system that installs on your existing gutters and excels at keeping small debris out—like pine needles and shingle grit. LeafGuard, on the other hand, is an entirely new gutter system that comes in one piece. This makes it hold up well over time, but might not repel fine particles as well.

Both systems offer long-term protection, but LeafFilter is the better choice if your gutters are in good shape and you just need a guard. LeafGuard is a full gutter replacement, making more sense if your gutters are worn out or failing.

Cost is another key difference. Both are on the expensive side of the market, but LeafFilter is the cheaper of the two. It runs about $3,000 to $7,000 on average, depending on your home’s size and roof complexity. Since LeafGuard is a full gutter replacement, it costs more—typically between $5,000 and $10,000.

This guide breaks down how each system works, what they cost, and why you might choose one over the other for your home.

My Take on LeafFilter Vs. LeafGuard

After performing a deep dive on LeafFilter vs. LeafGuard, my pick is LeafFilter, as the company ranked better in nearly every category. I’ve given LeafFilter the superlative “Best Professional Installation and Cost” for its pricing, detailed installation process, and durable three-piece system.

LeafFilter’s micro-mesh steel system is durable and corrosion-resistant. In addition to installing your new gutter guards, LeafFilter’s professionals will clean and seal your current gutters, nearly eliminating the cost of cleaning your gutters entirely. If you live in an area with pine trees, you’ll be happy to know that this brand was ranked in the top place for the top gutter guard for pine needles.

In contrast, LeafGuard, my choice for “Most Durable,” offers a simple one-piece gutter and gutter guard design. It’s better for homes with less functional or more heavily damaged gutters. LeafGuard’s quote includes the removal of old gutters, gutter guard installation, and future maintenance.

LeafFilter Vs. LeafGuard Cost

LeafFilter’s pricing is typically between $17 and $45 per linear foot, which includes a free inspection, gutter cleaning and repair, and gutter guard installation. Trained professionals install the guards directly over your existing gutters or they can install a new system.

Like most service-oriented companies, LeafFilter doesn’t offer flat rates or direct pricing information on its website. Instead, you’ll need an in-person inspection before receiving your custom quote. The exact cost can depend on home size, gutter damage, roof pitch, location, and more. LeafFilter also offers 10% senior and military discounts, which can help you save a healthy chunk of change if you qualify.

LeafGuard is less expensive than LeafFilter at $11 to $37 per linear foot. The price includes the home inspection and professional installation. Unlike LeafFilter, LeafGuard requires you to replace your whole gutter system.

I like that LeafGuard offers flexible financing plans for its products. As of this writing, for the $7,883 LeafGuard System, you might qualify for a 132-month (11-year) plan with $99 for installation and $99 monthly payments. Plus, the brand’s lifetime clog-free guarantee promises free cleaning in the event of clogged gutters.

Although LeafGuard costs less and you’re getting all new gutters, LeafFilter receives better reviews for its high-quality installation and product. I personally would choose this company despite its slightly higher price point because of the greater value it offers customers. However, I recommend getting a few quotes before making a decision.

LeafFilter Vs. LeafGuard Warranties

Both companies offer lifetime transferable warranties, which means the warranty lasts for the lifetime of your home and transfers to new owners if you decide to move. Also, both guarantee their product will prevent gutter clogs.

LeafFilter’s Warranty

LeafFilter’s warranty has the slogan “Clog-Free. Guaranteed.” If LeafFilter’s system ever allows your gutters to become clogged and overflow, the company will provide a replacement or refund 100% of your material purchase price.

The warranty doesn’t cover: 

  • Damage related to ice dams, plant life, or weather
  • Damage to your gutters, fascia board, or roof substrate during installation
  • Products that were modified or altered from its original installation
  • Overflows due to an insufficient number of downspouts

The homeowner is responsible for reporting any covered damage in writing to LeafFilter in a timely manner. The retailer might request additional information, such as photographs or a field inspection.

LeafGuard’s Warranty

LeafGuard is a proprietary brand with one-piece aluminum gutter guards that are said to “Get it. And forget it.” Its warranty states that as long as the surfaces of its gutter guard system are installed correctly and all cleaning methods have been applied properly, the product won’t experience any blistering, chipping, cracking, flaking, peeling, red rust, rotting, splitting, or structural deterioration.

While the warranty is transferable, a change in ownership reverts the warranty length to 50 years from the installation date. The warranty doesn’t cover:

  • Mold or mildew
  • Normal weathering
  • Physical abuse or misuse
  • Structural failures
  • Vandalism or accidental damage
  • Weather damage

LeafGuard offers relief in the form of repainting, replacement or repairing its product, where applicable.

What Gutter Guard Types Do LeafFilter and LeafGuard Offer?

LeafGuard and LeafFilter both offer gutter protection systems designed to prevent the buildup of debris such as leaves, pine needles and pests — and to ensure the free flow of rainwater. 

Between the two companies, I deem LeafFilter as the better product for its high-quality materials and how it blends in better with the home.

LeafFilter Gutter Guards

LeafFilter gutter guards are three-piece systems that allow water to flow through the gutters while preventing debris and leaves from clogging inside. Professionals can install the system over your existing gutters (if they fit) or install new gutters.

From an aesthetic and home value perspective, I appreciate that the LeafFilter gutter guards are less bulky and blend in better with the roof and any existing system.

LeafFilter’s professional installation includes the following:

  • Steel micro-mesh screen: 275-micron fine surgical-grade stainless steel guards won’t rust and they prevent small debris from entering your gutter system.
  • uPVC frame: This durable frame supports the micro-mesh screen at the gutter’s top but still allows unrestricted water flow.
  • Structural hangers: Installers place hidden hangers to secure the gutter guard system to the home’s fascia.
  • Surface tension: LeafFilter’s system has a built-in pitch that creates surface tension to keep water flowing and debris out.

LeafGuard’s Gutter Guards

LeafGuard has a reverse-curve design that causes falling debris to slide off the guard using water surface tension. The system has an extra thick aluminum shell that’s 20% thicker than the industry standard, making it a solid choice for stormy areas or homes with heavily damaged gutter systems. It’s also reinforced with non-corrosive brackets that fasten directly to the fascia board every 2 feet.

Each LeafGuard product has the following:

  • Aluminum reverse-curve design: The unique aluminum reverse-curve design creates surface tension and helps your gutter system handle heavy rainfall — up to 32 inches per hour. LeafGuard gutter guards also have extra large downspouts, making them ideal for rainy areas or gutter systems that clog easily.
  • Hidden hangers: Fitted hidden hangers are installed on the fascia board every 2 feet to keep them in place and away from roof shingles.
  • ScratchGuard paint: This patented paint is crack, chip, and peel-resistant to keep your gutter guard system looking nice for years.
  • Custom-fitting: Each LeafGuard gutter is custom-fit to your home.

How Do Services Compare Between LeafFilter and LeafGuard?

Regarding service and installation processes, LeafFilter and LeafGuard are on par with each other with no notable differences.

LeafFilter’s Services and Installation Process

LeafFilter’s installation process requires a professional installer certified for LeafFilter’s products. To start this process, contact your LeafFilter sales representative to schedule your free inspection. They’ll inspect your gutter system, measure the length of your gutters, and check for damage before creating a personalized estimate.

Next, you’ll schedule a time for the installation specialist to install your new LeafFilter gutter system. Many customers have noted that technicians were available for next-day installations, so this is often a speedy process. Upon arrival, the technicians will clean your gutters, fix any damaged or worn-out sections, and install your new gutter guards, which can take a few hours to an entire day, depending on the project’s scope.

All told, their installation process includes:

  • On-site cost estimation for installation after inspection
  • In-depth analysis of your gutter guard needs, including inspection of downspouts and current gutters
  • Assessment of potential high-debris areas to determine need for full or partial installation
  • Installation by trained technicians
  • Removal of ineffective gutter guards and installation of new gutters, if necessary

LeafGuard’s Services and Installation Process

LeafGuard’s installation process is a little more extensive because each gutter system is custom fit to the exact specifications of your house. Otherwise, the installation process is similar, with a certified professional coming to your home for a free evaluation and walk around. I personally like that LeafGuard’s installers also offer extra education on how the system works while performing the walk through.

The brand’s services include: 

  • On-site inspection and custom fabrication 
  • Disassembly and removal of old gutters
  • Installation by trained technicians
  • Measurement to ensure a perfect fit
  • Free cleaning under the company’s lifetime “no-clog guarantee”

LeafFilter Vs. LeafGuard Reviews

Like any gutter guard service provider, negative reviews exist for both LeafFilter and LeafGuard. Homeowners should look at trends and assess reviews on multiple third-party review platforms, such as Trustpilot and the Better Business Bureau (BBB). After reviewing hundreds of reviews for each company on several review websites, I would feel more comfortable purchasing from LeafFilter.

LeafFilter’s Reviews

LeafFilter has higher ratings and more reviews on trusted third-party platforms. For example, as of this writing, LeafFilter has an A+ BBB rating and a BBB consumer review rating of 3.79 out of 5 stars. 

Many customers highlighted their favorable experiences with the LeafFilter gutter system installation—specifically, that the quote process and repairs to their existing gutters were top-notch. Consumers also detailed an overall positive experience with the technicians and representatives, noting their friendliness, professionalism, and expertise. 

One positive BBB review posted in June 2024 states, “The precision of the cuts and joints were seamless. There were no visible gaps or seams anywhere. They tacked down the downspouts at the height I wanted and filled all the joints with silicone. They worked their tails off in the heat and cleaned up even better than it was before they arrived.”

Unfavorable reviews cite high prices, unreliable workmanship, and high-pressure sales tactics.

In a 3-star BBB review posted in June 2024, the customer wrote, “The salesman did not inspect preexisting gutters and overcharged for an estimate which was later reduced by someone up the chain.”

LeafGuard’s Reviews

In contrast, LeafGuard had mixed customer opinions. As of this writing, the brand has an A+ rating on the BBB, but BBB consumer reviews rate the company 1.49 out of 5 stars.

LeafGuard customers appreciate the product’s durability and effectiveness in preventing clogs. Many favorable reviews cite reduced frequency of maintenance and the satisfaction of knowing their gutters are protected year-round. They also discussed the excellent customer service they received from the representatives and installers.

A 5-star BBB review posted in October 2023 praised LeafGuard’s installation process and the crew. The same consumer said LeafGuard met its warranty obligations twice—once because of a leak and once because of warping.

On the other hand, many unfavorable BBB reviews cite high-pressure sales tactics. In a 1-star review posted in February 2024, a LeafGuard customer wrote, “The whole business is built on aggressive sales that prey on new homeowners just trying to protect their home, and older folks not wanting to go on their roofs but also want to maintain their home.”

Some unhappy customers also noted issues with the installation and excessive debris buildup after several years. While LeafGuard did send technicians to clean the gutters out, customers shared that the cleaning left much to be desired, with some even needing to call the company back.

Where Are LeafFilter and LeafGuard Available?

LeafFilter has a broader coverage area and more service locations than LeafGuard, with 47 states offering LeafFilter services. The company doesn’t serve:

  • South Dakota
  • Hawaii
  • Alaska

LeafGuard services 37 states. If you live in the following states, you won’t be able to use this company’s services for your gutter guard installation needs:

  • Alaska
  • Arizona
  • Delaware
  • Hawaii
  • Maine
  • Mississippi
  • Montana
  • Nevada
  • North Dakota
  • Rhode Island
  • South Dakota
  • West Virginia
  • Wyoming

If you live in Alaska, South Dakota, or Hawaii, neither LeafFilter or LeafGuard are available service providers.

So, Is LeafFilter or LeafGuard the Best?

A quality gutter guard system saves you hours of cleaning your gutters each year and reduces your risk of injury while working on a ladder. A proper gutter guard system can extend the life of your roof and foundation, saving you money in the long run on home repairs.

For me, LeafFilter is the best gutter service because of its more comprehensive lifetime warranty, better customer reviews, and multi-piece system, which can be installed on existing gutter systems. However, LeafGuard may be the best option if you live in an area with intense storms or heavy rainfall, as its thicker aluminum design can withstand more inclement weather.

I recommend considering your top priorities and gathering several free quotes from multiple providers before making your final decision. If you’re looking to make cleaning your gutters less of a headache, call LeafFilter and LeafGuard to get your free estimate.

FAQs About LeafFilter and LeafGuard

Which is more expensive, LeafGuard or LeafFilter?

LeafFilter is more expensive when it comes to the price per linear foot. However, LeafGuard’s one-piece system requires the entire gutter system to be replaced, so its prices can fluctuate and be more expensive, especially if you need a large gutter system.

Does LeafFilter cause ice dams?

No, LeafFilter doesn’t cause or prevent ice dams. Ice dams form at the roof’s edge, so a good gutter guard system can help divert water through the gutters and away from your home so it doesn’t freeze in the eavestrough.

What time of year should you buy gutter guards?

The best times of year to perform a DIY gutter installation or hire a professional gutter guard installer are August and September. Temperatures begin to drop, but it’s also early enough to avoid a significant onslaught of falling leaves, which become a nuisance during installation as the gutters must be completely clear.

Methodology: How I Evaluated LeafFilter and LeafGuard Against Our Review Standards

As a member of Today’s Homeowner’s team, I strive to bring you the most transparent and accurate information for your home improvement projects. My gutter guard ratings emphasize high-quality gutter guard systems that can keep your gutters debris-free for years.

My detailed ratings are based on publicly available information about each company, secret shopping online and over the phone, customer-review analysis, and interviews with former and current home improvement experts.

A gutter guard company can earn 100 points across six categories, converted to a five-star scale. I researched and analyzed LeafFilter and LeafGuard based on the following formula:

  • Product Overview (15 points): Micro-mesh gutter guards are the best on the market. They screen even the smallest debris from your gutters and typically have the structural integrity to withstand heavy rainfall and accumulated debris from trees and surrounding foliage. I used customer testimonials and in-house testing results to determine debris resistance. I also took into consideration multiple color and sizing options.
  • Services Offered (35 points): I rated gutter guard providers highly that offer a full range of services — gutter installation and removal, complimentary maintenance, and more are factored into this rating.
  • Affordability (15 points): Though getting cost estimates for gutter guards usually requires home visits, I ranked companies based on factors such as discount and financing programs, multiple easy payment options, and the increased value of complimentary maintenance.
  • Warranties (10 points): A company that stands behind its products and services typically offers material and workmanship warranties. I evaluated companies based on the comprehensiveness of each warranty.
  • Customer Service (10 points): I considered customer service availability and ease of communication.
  • Company Reputation (15 points): I looked into each company’s service record to determine how they treated clients and how they responded to customer complaints. Better Business Bureau (BBB) rating and complaint response rate were our primary metrics for this category.

We monitor company data on an ongoing basis to keep rankings and information up to date.
